newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in featureless trade, with activity limited by the upcoming Hari Raya Haji holiday tomorrow, dealers said on Thursday.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. international trade for February and weekly jobless claims data.
International trade for February is forecast to show a deficit of US$10.1 billion compared with a deficit of $12.71 billion reported in January.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended April 12 are expected to reach 317,000 against the previous week's 318,000.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for more clues to market direction from tonight's release of the international trade and weekly jobless claims figures," a local dealer said.
"But most people have squared their positions ahead of the Hari Raya Haji holiday on Friday, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent but weekend eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, six-months unchanged at 6 5-7/8 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-3/8 6-1/4 percent.
